title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a page of the 1976 notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. It is a typed page, p. 192, of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §14.2. It was most likely reused as scratch paper: the neighbouring pages are handwritten computations of homotopy of simplicial modules (K(k,i) via exterior powers of k^I/k).

The mathematics: K is the fraction field of a complete discrete valuation ring. A_K is an abelian variety with (potentially) semistable reduction. Raynaud's rigid uniformization (14.1.7) is an exact sequence of rigid-analytic group sheaves
0 → M_K^an → G_K^an → A_K^an → 0.
Here G_K is the Raynaud extension (a torus extended by an abelian variety with good reduction), M_K is an étale lattice (locally Z^r), and i: M_K → G_K is the period map.

Apply the long exact sequence of Ext^i(Z/n, −) on the rigid site over K. Hom(Z/n, M) = 0 because M is torsion-free, and Ext^1(Z/n, G) = 0 because G is n-divisible. Using Ext^1(Z/n, M) = M/nM, one gets
0 → nG^an → nA^an → (M/n)^an → 0.
All terms are finite K-group schemes, so this algebraizes to (14.2.1):
0 → nG_K → nA_K → M_{K,n} → 0.
Taking the limit over ℓ-powers gives (14.2.2):
0 → T_ℓ(G_K) → T_ℓ(A_K) → M_K ⊗ Z_ℓ → 0.

The algebraic theory of §8 (Néron models and monodromy) already provides (14.2.3):
- T_ℓ(G_K) ≅ T_ℓ(A_K)^{ef}, the essentially fixed part (fixed by an open subgroup of inertia);
- T_ℓ/T_ℓ^{ef} ≅ M_K ⊗ Z_ℓ, via the orthogonality theorem and the character group of the toric part of the dual.

Grothendieck asserts that the algebraic and transcendental (rigid) filtrations coincide. For the first map he argues by reduction to the semistable case. The page breaks off mid-sentence. The purpose is to relate the period lattice of Raynaud's uniformization to the monodromy pairing.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. The surjectivity in the n-torsion sequence correctly uses the n-divisibility of G_K^an as a sheaf (Ext^1(Z/n, G) = G/nG = 0), and Hom(Z/n, M) = 0 from torsion-freeness.
The argument for the first homomorphism is cut off at the page end; the rest is presumably on the next page of SGA 7 IX, not included here.

ideas.what: n-torsion and Tate-module exact sequences deduced from rigid uniformization 0→M→G→A→0
ideas.modern_name: Raynaud (Mumford–Tate) uniformization; Tate module filtration T(G) ⊂ T(A) with quotient M⊗Z_ℓ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (curves), Mumford (1972), Raynaud (1970/71), Grothendieck SGA 7 IX

ideas.what: Comparison of the algebraic filtration T^{ef} (from Néron models/monodromy) with the transcendental one from rigid uniformization
ideas.modern_name: compatibility of the monodromy filtration with Raynaud uniformization

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX, apparently used as scratch paper behind the 1976 handwritten notes. Its content is fully published and credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: The page is a typescript page of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, p. 192 (archive stamp 510), not part of the handwritten 1976 notes; the handwritten neighbours are unrelated simplicial-homotopy computations.
In the title, the target of i is G_K (written in a fancy font), the same object as G_K in the text, not a separate 𝔾_K.
The 'ef' superscript denotes the 'essentiellement fixe' part of T_ℓ(A_K).
